topic: How often meat is found in Vietnamese chay
claim_a: Can Tho University kit paper: there have been many cases of meat detected in vegetarian foods through process failure or mixing [CHY-61]
claim_b: Press and enforcement record 2015 to 2026: no confirmed case; one 2021 seizure on suspicion with no published result [TRU-18; TRU-22; LBL-23; LBL-24]
position_taken: Frequency is unmeasured; treat fake chay as a latent rumour and screen for it cheaply within DMV-07
notes: The CTU paper tested no market samples

topic: Whether soy protein is a positive or a negative
claim_a: Health media and suppliers: soy is 'boneless meat', 25 g a day recommended, a functional meat ingredient [TRU-22; TRU-23; TRU-28]
claim_b: Artisan sellers: 'no soy protein filler' as a quality claim [TRU-27]
position_taken: Both hold in different contexts: soy is positive as a food and neutral when listed in industrial sausages; negative when hidden, cost-driven or in products sold on purity
notes: Snippet evidence on the seller side

topic: Taiwanese fake-chay figures relayed in Vietnam
claim_a: VietNamNet 2015: 70% (15 of 21) of Taiwanese imitation-meat samples contained animal products [TRU-01]
claim_b: Same article: Taiwan FDA found labelled packs mostly compliant and 4 of 15 loose samples with pork or chicken [TRU-01]
position_taken: Do not use either figure for Vietnam; they show only that the story circulated

topic: First fine-emulsion format for the TPP-03 test
claim_a: W8-L6: one fine emulsion, giò lụa or xúc xích, plus one coarse format
claim_b: This line: industrial xúc xích, not giò lụa, because giò lụa's public quality test is the absence of starch and 2019 extension was read as cheating [TRU-02; TRU-03; TRU-27]
position_taken: Xúc xích first; giò lụa only after a label test
notes: Texture limits in W8-L6 (HXE-01) point the same way

topic: Whether mixed-protein meat products carry a label penalty
claim_a: Part VI ch24.4: mixed-protein products from the largest processors sell at mass scale without a label penalty [BUY-05]
claim_b: 2019: starch extension of market giò cost sellers customers and was called dishonest [TRU-03]
position_taken: Both hold: the penalty falls on hidden cost-cutting in artisan channels, not on listed soy in branded lines
